description.text: CNA Financial Corporation (CNAF) was incorporated in 1967 and is an insurance holding company. References to “CNA,” “the Company,” “we,” “our,” “us” or like terms refer to the business of CNAF and its subsidiaries. CNA's property and casualty and remaining life and group insurance operations are primarily conducted by Continental Casualty Company (CCC), The Continental Insurance Company, Western Surety Company, CNA Insurance Company Limited, Hardy Underwriting Bermuda Limited and its subsidiaries (Hardy), and CNA Insurance Company (Europe) S.A. Loews Corporation (Loews) owned approximately 92% of our outstanding common stock as of December 31, 2025. Our insurance products primarily include commercial property and casualty coverages, including surety. Our services include warranty, risk management information services and claims administration. Our products and services are primarily marketed through independent agents, retail and wholesale brokers and managing general underwriters to a wide variety of customers, including small, medium and large businesses, insurance companies, associations, professionals and other groups. The property and casualty insurance industry is highly competitive, both as it relates to rate and service. We compete with a large number of stock and mutual insurance companies, as well as other entities, for both distributors and customers.

about.description_short: CNA is one of the largest U.S. commercial property and casualty insurance companies. Backed by more than 125 years of experience, CNA provides a broad range of standard and specialized insurance products and services for businesses and professionals in the U.S., Canada and Europe.

analysis_md:
# CNA — CNA Financial Corporation
v5 run, engine 5.4.0, 2026-10-18. Market cap $13.048B at $47.90 (nasdaq_quote_api, dcf_numbers.json) — in scope under $40B.

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, or the cited company releases — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Chicago-based commercial property & casualty insurer (SIC 6331, Fire, Marine & Casualty Insurance, per fundamentals.json), the seventh-largest U.S. commercial insurer, ~92% owned by Loews Corporation — a controlled company with a thin public float. Core P&C segments are Specialty, Commercial and International, plus a Life & Group segment carrying long-term-care runoff and a Corporate & Other segment carrying legacy mass-tort / asbestos liabilities. FY2025 (company Q4 2025 release): P&C net written premiums $10,683M (+5%), net earned premiums $10,478M (+7%), underwriting gain $551M, P&C combined ratio 94.7% (underlying 91.8%), full-year net income $4.69/share and core income $4.93/share; a $2.00/share special dividend was declared with Q4 2025 and the regular quarterly dividend raised 4% to $0.48. AM Best upgraded the financial strength rating to A+ (stable) in December 2025. Q2 2026 (company release): net income $321M ($1.18/share), core income $1.19/share, P&C net written premiums +4% to $2,970M with new business +11% to a record $718M and retention 83%, but the P&C combined ratio deteriorated to 96.5% (underlying 94.2%, vs 91.7% a year earlier) and Corporate & Other again took a $77M after-tax charge for unfavorable legacy mass-tort development ($88M in Q2 2025).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $2,490,000,000; capex $86,000,000; SBC $41,000,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense — always a real cost, and trivial here).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $2,363,000,000 = $8.67474302496329/share** (dcf_numbers.json base_oe_total_latest_fy / base_oe_latest_per_share).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $1,278,000,000 — exactly net income, and barely half the conservative figure. That gap is the central fact of this file (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE): for a P&C insurer the OCF-based figure capitalizes float — premiums collected and reserves accrued ahead of claims paid — which belongs to future policyholders, not owners.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json). Net debt $2,546,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json, basis LongTermDebtNoncurrent+none), 1.0774439272111722× normalized OE (diagnostics) — a holding-company figure only; the real balance sheet (fundamentals.json, FY2025) is assets $69,443,000,000 against liabilities $57,822,000,000 and equity $11,621,000,000, book value $42.66/share at YE2025; the Q2 2026 release reports book value $41.34/share, $45.83 excluding AOCI.
- Share count is essentially flat (diluted 272,400,000 latest; share CAGR −0.00012231122115691218/yr) — Loews' stake means buybacks are minimal ($36M TTM per fundamentals.json); capital return runs through the regular + special dividends instead.

**Base used = the engine's normalized base: $8.67474302496329/share, median of the last 3 FY OE/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the three years are $7.9243203526818515 / $8.925559222588925 / $8.67474302496329 per financials_history.csv). No TTM base was used: ttm.py exited non-zero with the exact message "ttm.py: cannot compute TTM for CNA (CIK 21175): sbc: no post-FY YTD fact (no 10-Q since the 2025-12-31 fiscal year end)" — CNA has filed 10-Qs through Q2 2026 (fundamentals.json latest 10-Q filed 2026-08-03, period 2026-06-30), but its 10-Q YTD SBC fact is not tagged in companyfacts (fundamentals.json quarterly SBC is null in every quarter), so this is a tooling/tagging failure on the SBC leg, not a filing-data gap in the annual history. The fundamentals.json TTM through Q2 2026 corroborates the median base's direction rather than contradicting it: TTM operating cash flow $2,332,000,000 is BELOW FY2025's $2,490,000,000 (OCF YoY −12.03%), TTM net income $1,237,000,000 vs $1,278,000,000 in FY2025, TTM revenue $15,151,000,000 (+3.41% YoY) — the FY-based median is, if anything, generous, and is treated throughout as an upper bound because of the float problem below.

**Revenue-tag caveat (affects the growth blend):** the engine's revenue series uses RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, which captures only a fee/contract slice of an insurer's top line — $1,577,000,000 in FY2025 in financials_history.csv vs the filer's total revenue of $14,989,000,000 in fundamentals.json (premiums earned and net investment income are not contract revenue). The engine's revenue growth components (5y CAGR 0.04724481146344783, 3y CAGR 0.0006347759327185454, latest YoY −0.019888129272840227) therefore describe that slice, not the company. True top-line growth (fundamentals.json): revenue +7.30% in FY2024 and +5.04% in FY2025, TTM +3.41%; P&C net written premiums +5% in FY2025 decelerating to +4% in Q2 2026 with renewal premium change down to +2% and renewal rate flat (Q2 2026 release/coverage). The blended g_base of 0.02350160117959471 inherits the broken revenue inputs but lands in a defensible range against those decelerating true prints — see the growth sanity check under DCF.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-narrow
Justification: a scaled, A+-rated specialty/commercial franchise with genuine underwriting expertise, but P&C cover is re-bid at renewal through non-exclusive brokers/agents, pricing power belongs to the industry cycle rather than to CNA, and measured returns sit at the cost of capital through the cycle — ROE (fundamentals.json annual) ran 5.43% (2020), 10.66% (2021), 7.98% (2022), 12.18% (2023), 9.12% (2024), 11.00% (2025), i.e. around, not well above, the cost of capital. fundamentals.json reports no gross margin and a null roic_proxy for this insurer (no filed operating-income series), so ROE and the combined ratio are the return evidence: FY2025 combined 94.7% / underlying 91.8% is competent, not elite (elite underwriters run high-80s/low-90s all-in), and the underlying combined ratio deteriorated to 94.2% in Q2 2026. That evidence supports 4, not the 7+ the rubric reserves for franchises earning well above capital costs through a cycle.
- FOR: scale — seventh-largest U.S. commercial insurer with Specialty / Commercial / International breadth (company disclosures); AM Best A+ financial strength (upgraded December 2025) supporting broker and policyholder trust; specialty expertise in professional liability, surety (Western Surety) and healthcare lines where underwriting skill differentiates; expense ratio held below 30% (29.7% FY2025, company release) while investing in technology/AI; retention 83% with new business +11% to a record $718M in Q2 2026; Loews' ~92% ownership as a historically supportive, long-horizon parent.
- AGAINST: commodity cover re-shopped at renewal — policyholder switching costs are low and distribution is intermediated and non-exclusive; far larger rivals (Chubb, Travelers, AIG) set the competitive terms; pricing is cyclical and now softening (renewal rate flat in Q2 2026); social inflation is pressuring loss ratios (underlying loss ratio up across segments in 2026); recurring legacy mass-tort/asbestos charges in Corporate & Other ($77M after-tax in Q2 2026 alone, $88M in Q2 2025) and LTC runoff in Life & Group are permanent-looking drags on group earnings; catastrophe tail (2.3 points of Q2 2026 combined ratio); controlled-company structure — minority holders have no governance say and the float is thin.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — v5 final run (engine 5.4.0, 2026-10-18)
Default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10, default growth offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp, default OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25, moat 4. Price $47.90.
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** scenario starts are −9.65% / −2.65% / **+2.35%** / +7.35% / +14.35%. Against actual recent prints — total revenue +5.04% FY2025 and +3.41% TTM (fundamentals.json), P&C net written premiums +5% FY2025 → +4% Q2 2026, Q2 2026 revenue +1.9% YoY — the base start (+2.35%) sits BELOW the latest prints for a written reason: premium growth is decelerating, renewal pricing has gone flat, and the underlying combined ratio is deteriorating (91.8% FY2025 → 94.2% Q2 2026), so trailing growth overstates the forward starting point; the bear/super-bear negative starts are the reserve-charge / catastrophe-year cases this insurer periodically prints in earnings terms. The bull start (+7.35%) is above trailing prints and is a genuine bull assumption (pricing re-hardening plus investment-income compounding), not a description of today. The super-bull start (+14.35%) exceeds every recent print — it is a 10%-weighted tail (hard market + reserve releases + portfolio returns), not a forecast, and the verdict is not sized to it. The blend did not hit the 35% cap, so no recalibration was needed.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −9.65% | 0.75 | Major reserve strengthening (mass tort/asbestos) + cat year + soft pricing | $33.18 | 10.80% |
| Bear | 25% | −2.65% | 0.90 | Pricing softens further, underlying combined grinds toward 96-97%, legacy charges persist | $52.44 | 16.25% |
| Base | 30% | +2.35% | 1.00 | Low-single-digit premium growth, combined ~95%, float-carrying OCF base held flat in real terms | $70.72 | 20.97% |
| Bull | 25% | +7.35% | 1.10 | Pricing re-hardens, new-business momentum compounds, investment income grows | $94.18 | 26.36% |
| Super bull | 10% | +14.35% | 1.25 | Sustained hard market + reserve releases + strong portfolio returns (tail case) | $139.18 | 35.10% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $75.11 (+56.80% vs price), IV@12% $99.24, IV@10% $126.10, IV@20% $53.33, IV@25% $41.28, weighted IRR 21.95%, base-case IRR 20.97%**
- **Tier by numbers: A.** Bear→bull band: B (16.25%) → S (26.36%). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 18.11%, terminal value 18.20% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.19×, net debt 1.08× normalized OE, 9.56 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): ttm.py was run and failed — exact message quoted in the OE section (SBC YTD leg untagged in the 10-Qs). Per the v5 rules the engine's median base is used instead, with that reason stated; the fundamentals.json TTM through Q2 2026 (OCF $2,332,000,000, below FY2025; net income $1,237,000,000, roughly flat) confirms the median is not stale in a flattering direction.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): structural for this insurer, not a single one-off. From financials_history.csv: 2023 OCF $2,285,000,000 vs net income $1,205,000,000; 2024 OCF $2,571,000,000 vs net income $959,000,000; 2025 OCF $2,490,000,000 vs net income $1,278,000,000. D&A ($73,000,000 / $67,000,000 / $70,000,000) explains none of it. The cause is insurance mechanics: premiums are collected in cash up front while loss reserves and unearned premiums accrue unpaid (float), and non-cash reserve charges — including the recurring legacy mass-tort development in Corporate & Other — depress net income without consuming operating cash. Consequence: the OCF-based conservative OE ($2,363,000,000 in FY2025) is roughly double the maintenance/N-I-based figure ($1,278,000,000) because it capitalizes float that is owed to future claimants. Neither raw series is clean earning power; the OCF base is an upper bound, which is exactly why the final tier is softened one notch and confidence is low.

## My thoughts / overlay
- **Method range is the headline, as with every insurer in this sweep:** the engine's raw OCF-median base produces Tier A (weighted IRR 21.95%, IV@15% $75.11). Every earnings-based way of looking at CNA lands lower, because roughly half the OCF base is float/reserve accrual rather than distributable earnings (FY2025 conservative OE $2,363,000,000 vs maintenance OE $1,278,000,000). The defensible range is B-or-lower on earnings lenses to A on the raw engine, with the A end resting entirely on the cash-flow definition the sector flag rejects. The verdict is sized to the conservative end: B, low confidence.
- Quality is not the debate: underwriting has been profitable (combined <100% through the cycle, 94.7% in FY2025), the A+ rating was just upgraded, the expense ratio is controlled below 30%, new business is growing double digits, and capital return is real ($2.00 special dividend plus a raised regular dividend in February 2026). The debate is the multiple for a controlled, mid-tier commercial insurer whose pricing tailwind is fading (renewal rate flat, underlying combined +2.5 points YoY in Q2 2026) and whose legacy tail keeps charging.
- Red flags to monitor: further legacy mass-tort / asbestos development in Corporate & Other (a charge in both Q2 2025 and Q2 2026), social-inflation-driven loss-ratio drift in Commercial, LTC runoff in Life & Group, catastrophe severity, investment-portfolio credit in a downturn, and the Loews control overhang (any Loews sell-down changes the float/governance picture entirely).
- **Hurdle math:** on the engine's numbers the stock clears a 15% IRR at $75.11 (the weighted IV@15%) and trades 56.80% below that figure at $47.90 — but that clearing price inherits the float-inflated base and overstates the true margin of safety; the bear-case IV@15% of $52.44 sits only ~9% above the price, which is the honest cushion on the conservative end. On the final-tier B reading, the claim is "clears 15% with room on engine numbers, sized like a B", not "57% upside".
